key_insight: MAS-PINN uses shared temporal features and network structure to model coupled agents while reducing computational and memory costs.
engineering_relevance: The approach could make simulation, trajectory reconstruction, and physical-parameter identification more practical for large, partially observed multi-agent systems.
method: Represent trajectories with shared temporal features and agent-specific coefficients.
Alternate feature learning, coupled-trajectory fitting, and physical-parameter estimation.
Exploit local interactions through matrix-free coefficient updates.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Lorenz rings, Lotka–Volterra networks, and Rössler oscillators report improved trajectory and parameter accuracy over baselines, plus substantial savings in coefficient fitting.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify speedups or establish performance on real-world systems beyond the tested dynamical models.
paper_title: Efficient Modeling of Multi-Agent Systems via Structure-Aware Physics-Informed Learning
